source.signature: from the signature it is passed to

voidReason.constructor: a constructor's result is the instance, and `return` in it is only an early exit
voidReason.setter: a setter's result is discarded, and `return` in it is only an early exit
voidReason.annotatedVoid: its return type is `{{written}}` (from its annotation), which says `void`
voidReason.signatureVoid: its return type is `{{written}}` (from the signature it is passed to), which says `void`
voidReason.inferredVoid: its return type is `{{written}}` (inferred from its returns), which says `void`

bareReturnInValueFunction.text: This {{functionKind}} returns a value: its return type is `{{rendered}}` (<<source>>), so a bare `return;` hides that this path hands back `undefined`. Write `return undefined;`. A bare return is reserved for functions whose type says `void`, so a reader can tell at the return which kind of function this is.

undefinedReturnInVoidFunction.text: This {{functionKind}} returns nothing: <<voidReason>>, so `return undefined;` dresses an early exit up as a value. Write `return;`. `return undefined;` is reserved for functions whose type includes `undefined` as a value, so a reader can tell at the return which kind of function this is.
